title: Ruth Fenton, Stafford House Study Holidays
summary_en: This week, The PIE sat down with Ruth Fenton, founder and director of Stafford House Study Holidays. We spoke about building her business, the challenges facing young people and global policy shifts.
author: The PIE News team
title_cn: Ruth Fenton, Stafford House Study Holidays

title: US students’ study abroad appetite holds strong
summary_en: Two new surveys have found strong demand for study abroad among US students, even as global conflicts and financial barriers weigh heavily on decision-making.
author: Polly Nash
title_cn: US students’ study abroad appetite holds strong

title: Survey highlights gaps in universities’ international recruitment strategies
summary_en: New research presented at the Explore UK Forum by student recruitment platform Cialfo, part of Manifest Global, highlights three gaps in how universities recruit internationally, based on survey findings shared at the event.
author: Diya Singh
title_cn: Survey highlights gaps in universities’ international recruitment strategies

title: Is Andy Burnham going to save UK higher ed?
summary_en: If Andy Burnham becomes Prime Minister, will he save UK higher education? That was one question at this year's BUILA conference, where panellists delivered a dose of realism.
author: Kim Martin
title_cn: Is Andy Burnham going to save UK higher ed?

title: Modi meets with Australian higher ed as Flinders announces India campus
summary_en: Flinders University is set to open a campus in Bengaluru, India, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has revealed during Narendra Modi's visit to the country.
author: Beth Kennedy
title_cn: Modi meets with Australian higher ed as Flinders announces India campus

title: 60% of US colleges report fall in international applications
summary_en: Nearly six in 10 US colleges have seen a drop in international applications for 2026/27, driven by a sharp decline in interest from Indian students.
author: Polly Nash
title_cn: 60% of US colleges report fall in international applications

title: Students left in limbo weeks after Irish language school closes
summary_en: Irish stakeholders have called for urgent clarity as English language students studying at a school in Limerick are left in the dark weeks after its apparent closure.
author: Beth Kennedy
title_cn: Students left in limbo weeks after Irish language school closes

title: Germany adds new test to pre-visa checks for Indian master’s applicants
summary_en: The Digital Master Test (dMAT) will become a mandatory part of APS documentation for selected Indian master's applicants from the summer semester 2027.
author: Abhishek Nair
title_cn: Germany adds new test to pre-visa checks for Indian master’s applicants

title: Protecting students, supporting staff, strengthening the sector: a call for unified leadership
summary_en: The UK higher education sector has always been resilient. We have weathered political shifts, policy swings, and waves of public scrutiny. We have adapted, innovated, and continued to welcome students who enrich our campuses, communities, and economy. But today, something feels different, write Diana Beech and Sandy Bhangal.
author: Diana Beech and Sandy Bhangal
title_cn: Protecting students, supporting staff, strengthening the sector: a call for unified leadership

title: Italy launches €420m international mobility program for schools
summary_en: Government-backed program will fund overseas language learning and school immersion for 150,000 Italian upper secondary students as part of what the government describes as the country's largest international mobility program for schools.
author: Abhishek Nair
title_cn: Italy launches €420m international mobility program for schools

title: Irish stakeholders hail progress on ‘sex for rent’ legal crackdown
summary_en: Stakeholders in Ireland have welcomed progress on upcoming laws that will make 'sex for rent' a criminal offence, as the government moves to put an end to sexual harrassment when seeking housing.
author: Beth Kennedy
title_cn: Irish stakeholders hail progress on ‘sex for rent’ legal crackdown

title: How Australia is losing at international education
summary_en:
"Australia’s international education sector should be a global powerhouse, but there is instead a story of squandered promise," writes Felix Pirie, CEO of the
Independent Tertiary Education Council Australia (ITECA).
author: Felix Pirie
title_cn: How Australia is losing at international education
